name: Chesterfield

licensing.selective: No selective licensing scheme is listed on the council's website.
licensing.additional: No additional HMO licensing: only mandatory licensing of HMOs with five or more people from two or more households. Licences usually last five years and the council publishes a register.

neighbourhoods.name: Chesterfield town centre
neighbourhoods.housing: Victorian terraces and flats above shops around the market and the Crooked Spire, with some newer apartment blocks.

neighbourhoods.name: Brampton
neighbourhoods.housing: Long streets of Victorian and Edwardian terraces west of the centre, many let privately.

neighbourhoods.name: Walton
neighbourhoods.housing: Inter-war and post-war semis and detached houses in a mainly owner-occupied suburb.

neighbourhoods.name: Newbold
neighbourhoods.housing: A mix of inter-war semis, post-war council-built estates and Victorian terraces.

neighbourhoods.name: Whittington Moor
neighbourhoods.housing: Victorian and early 20th-century terraces near the A61, with newer homes on former industrial land.

neighbourhoods.name: Staveley
neighbourhoods.housing: A former mining and ironworks town with terraces, post-war council-built estates and new homes on regeneration land.

neighbourhoods.name: Brimington
neighbourhoods.housing: Mainly semis and bungalows from the mid 20th century with some older terraces.

neighbourhoods.name: Hasland
neighbourhoods.housing: Former mining village of terraces with post-war and modern estates around it.

housing: Chesterfield's housing is mostly Victorian and early 20th-century terraces near the centre, with large inter-war and post-war estates, a sizeable council-owned stock, and mining-era terraces in Staveley and Hasland. House prices are well below the national average and private renting is mainly two and three-bedroom terraces and semis. Some HMOs exist around the town centre and Brampton. New homes are being built on former industrial land at Staveley and along the Chesterfield Canal.
checkinTips: Victorian terraces in Brampton and Newbold: photograph the cellar for damp, the back yard and any shared passageway or gennel.
Older terraces: check sash or replacement windows, chimney breasts and loft hatches for signs of leaks.
Former mining areas such as Staveley and Hasland: photograph any cracks in walls and around frames so movement can be compared later.
Flats above shops in the town centre: note the separate entrance, stairs, fire alarm and meter cupboard locations.
Post-war semis and former council houses: record gardens, fences, sheds and the boiler and consumer unit.
HMOs near the centre: photograph each room's lock and fire door and note shared kitchen appliances one by one.
tenantHelp: Tenants in private rented homes can report disrepair or unsafe conditions to Chesterfield Borough Council's private sector housing team, which can inspect and enforce standards.
